verdict_on_ladder:
Most of the ladder does not hold up as a way to move the campaigns' task metrics. Four parts survive.

**The premise is not supported by the evidence.** The dossier's own attribution scoreboard (DOSSIER §4.8, lines 680-692) blames none of the four campaign metrics on the optimizer. Those metrics are tracking/turning, obstacle completion, formation rate and omni side speed. The only row it attributes to algorithm or hyper-parameters is motion quality (chatter, stand stepping, the 3-feet pattern). The dossier says so directly: task-metric limitation "is absent either way" (DOSSIER:993).

**Saturation is the same in every head, good or bad.** All 303 evaluated checkpoints are 91-100 % saturated. That includes the heads of record, which have turn facing 0.787 and obstacle completion 0.64-0.66. Fast and slow side heads are both 0.941-0.978 saturated. A property that never varies cannot explain why task metrics vary.

**The levers that did move task metrics were reward, curriculum, structure and plant changes:**
- turn facing +0.20 to +0.33;
- side speed 2.2-2.6× from single-direction training or the canonicaliser;
- obstacle onsets 2-3× from morphology.

The only optimizer change ever tried, M1, cost turn facing 0.100.

**The literature agrees.** Bounded heads change action geometry reliably but task return inconsistently: −22 % to +30 % on MuJoCo, and the legged results have weak seed statistics. Near-bang-bang control is the expected optimum for this plant, whose rods are slew-limited and cams acceleration-limited, under this reward's unsquared, L1-like action_rate cost.

**Rung 2, as written, also changes the reward.** A CPU Monte Carlo I ran estimates the extra action_rate cost from exploration noise on a bounded head at 0.68-1.44 per second. That is 1.6-5.8× the per-second margin between the fast and slow side gaits. In this repo, smoothness penalties have traded obstacle/terrain completion away monotonically.

**What survives, and why:**
- **Rung 0 (telemetry and defect fixes, 0 GPU-h).** Every later reading, including the reward campaigns', needs KL, clip fraction, explained variance and saturation logging.
- **Rung 1 (throughput probe, 0.5 GPU-h), with rung 4 folded into it.** More envs is an infrastructure change, not a hyper-parameter screen.
- **Rung 7 (canonical training), moved to first place.** It is the only rung with a large task effect to aim at (0.03-0.10 vs 0.18-0.22 m/s). It is already shown to work without training: the canonicaliser makes 4 of 4 fast heads fast on both hands. It also works whichever PPO mechanism turns out to be right. It is a structural change, not an algorithm change.
- **A smaller rung 2.** Run only the combined cell (bounded mean plus a σ that gets gradient), not the 2×2. Treat it as a motion-quality and sim-to-real test that must not lose task performance, not as a task-metric screen. Handle the action_rate confound first and use pre-registered early kill checks. The real reason to keep it is hardware: non-backdrivable rods chatter at 2.23 sign flips per dimension per second at stand. The four sim metrics do not measure that.

**What gets demoted or cut:**
- Rung 3 (step size) and the critic-learning-rate part of rung 5 run only if their conditions are met.
- Rung 6 (symmetry) runs after rung 7 and drops its M_y images.
- Rung 8 (γ 0.995) is cut.
- Rung 9's trigger is inverted: geometry without a task gain means stop, not escalate.

Roughly 30-33 of the ladder's 50-60 GPU-h can be cut or deferred on this evidence. Separately, the headline budget leaves out the lineage-length confirmation any adoption would need: about 45-100 GPU-h more (omni 12k at about 5.4 GPU-h per seed; forward 1a→2c at 7-10 per seed, plus re-distilling the student).

findings.finding: None of the four campaign task metrics is attributed to the optimizer. Saturation is the same in every trained head, good or bad, so it cannot explain differences in tracking/turning, obstacle completion, formation or side speed. The levers that did move those metrics were reward, curriculum, structure and plant changes. The one optimizer change ever made moved them the wrong way.
findings.evidence:
DOSSIER §4.8 (DOSSIER.md:680-692):
- The only ALG/HP row is 'Chatter, stand stepping, 3-feet pattern'.
- Two-direction side slowness is STRUCTURE, and optimizer telemetry does not separate the classes ('No (complete overlap)').
- The glide and the creeper are REWARD/TASK.
- The early lottery is STRUCTURE.
- Late regressions are CONFOUNDED.
- Stage-boundary collapse is a value-side issue.

The dossier's own words: 'Evidence that it limits task metrics ... is absent either way' (DOSSIER.md:993).

Saturation (DOSSIER.md:298-306, 515):
- 303/303 checkpoints at 999+ iterations are 0.91-1.00 saturated, including W (97.0 %, turn facing 0.787 after c6x) and the forward heads (0.99; obstacles 0.64-0.66).
- The 17 side-bisect heads are 0.941-0.978, fast and slow alike.
- Executing with training noise barely changes speed: stochastic vs deterministic vx 0.145 vs 0.151 (DOSSIER.md:514).

Levers that moved task metrics:
- Reward: KRABBY_YAW_PROGRESS_W=3.0 took turn facing 0.419→0.748 (facing_tracking_ladder/CHANGELOG.md:72).
- Curriculum: C1d took it 0.419→0.618 (:89).
- Clock cut c6x: 0.475→0.787 (2026-09-23_clock_deprecation_w2/REPORT.md:163), with the LR at the floor 61-64 % of the time (DOSSIER.md:468-469).
- fa mirror + scalar obs: side 0.084 → 0.184-0.217 m/s (DOSSIER.md:639).
- Morphology: obstacles 0.31 vs 0.69-0.95 (DOSSIER.md:408).

The only optimizer lever, M1 (σ cap 0.5):
- turn facing 0.610→0.510, move_turn facing 0.411→0.301, move_turn ratio 0.504→0.433 WORSE (MQ REPORT.md:181-254);
- tracking income 0.61 vs 0.69, episode length 1629 vs 1758 (ANALYSIS_M1_saturation.md:27-30).

PPO 'delivers the added-reward dose as predicted' (OS11, DOSSIER.md:556), and the glide out-earns the target (DOSSIER.md:522-523): the optimizer does maximise the reward it is given.
findings.recommended_change: Re-frame the ladder as exploratory, with no prior of task-metric gains. Pre-register a predicted direction for every task metric on every rung. Justify rung 2 by motion quality and sim-to-real chatter, with task metrics as non-inferiority guards, not as its expected payoff.

findings.finding: Rung 2, as specified, changes the reward economy as well as the head. action_rate penalises the L2 norm of the change in the clipped, delayed action. A saturated head hides its exploration noise from this term, and a bounded head cannot. Formation and tracking are therefore expected to get worse for reward reasons, not optimizer reasons, which would read as a misleading negative. Saturation itself is partly the policy escaping this tax.
findings.evidence:
Code:
- The reward is `torch.norm(prev[1]-prev[0])` on `raw_actions`, unsquared by default (P/parkour_isaaclab/envs/mdp/rewards.py:315-340).
- raw_actions come from the action history, which stores clipped actions (crab_hex_forward_task/mdp/parkour_actions.py:349-354), after the wrapper clamp (P/scripts/rsl_rl/vecenv_wrapper.py:134-136).
- Weight −0.3 on W (logs/rsl_rl/crab_hex_omni_flat_walk/2026-09-25_14-53-27_seed3_X03_c6x_A15pB/params/env.yaml:1789).

My CPU Monte Carlo (18 dims, clip ±1, noise only), cost per second = 0.3·E‖Δa‖:

| head | cost/s |
|---|---|
| W-like, median \|μ\| 11.2, σ 2 | 0.047 |
| bounded \|μ\| ≤ 1.1, σ 0.5 | 0.73 |
| bounded, σ 1.0 | 1.16 |
| bounded, σ 2.0 | 1.49 |
| formation-like, \|μ\| ~1, σ 1.65 | 1.22 |

So saturating frees about 1.2/s of income.

Comparisons:
- The fast side gait earns only +0.25 to +0.43/s more than slow (ROOT_CAUSE.md:258-268).
- In the omni creeper replay the ordering was decided by penalties: action_rate −0.516 vs −0.198, foot_idle −1.747 vs −0.441; walker net 0.095/s vs 1.503/s (DOSSIER.md:546-552).
- In-repo, smoothness taxes traded completion monotonically: L2 completion 0.81, L3 0.64 vs baked 0.90-0.94, 'churn is load-bearing' (crab_hex_forward_task/experiments/2026-08-22_1200_gait_formation_v2/CHANGELOG.md:49).
- Also cited: DOSSIER.md:497 'action_rate penalty rewards saturation'.
findings.recommended_change:
Before any rung-2 GPU run, pass the house offline reward-replay gate on a bounded-noise regime.

Then do one of two things:
- apply one pre-registered action_rate change (for example computing it on the deterministic mean, or a matched weight) to BOTH the incumbent and the bounded cell; or
- state explicitly that rung 2 measures head plus reward together.

Add a control cell with the action_rate change alone if rung 2 shows any task-metric difference.

findings.finding: Rung 7 is the ladder's strongest rung and is placed last-but-two, after about 35-45 GPU-h of rungs with no task-metric prior. It is a structural fix, not an algorithm change. It is the only rung aimed at a large-effect task failure, it has a proof without training, and it works whichever PPO failure mechanism turns out to be right. It survives, and it should run first.
findings.evidence:
- Every network trained on both hands is SLOW or DEAD at 0.028-0.103 m/s; one-direction heads are 0.184-0.217 m/s (DOSSIER.md:568-571).
- The exact M_y canonicaliser makes 4/4 fast heads FAST on both hands with no training, |L−R| ≤ 0.006 (DOSSIER.md:572; ROOT_CAUSE.md:270-279).
- ROOT_CAUSE says canonical training 'is expected FAST under every candidate' and 'can run at any point' (ROOT_CAUSE.md:467-470, 473-481).
- Capacity is ruled out: distillation reaches 99 % sign agreement (ROOT_CAUSE.md:183-190).
- The lit review ranks it 7th (lit-review-rl-algorithm-and-ppo-hyperparameters.md:587-591).
findings.recommended_change:
Promote to the first GPU rung, after rung 0. Start with C_lr_canon s3 (~1.2 GPU-h).

Kill criteria:
- **Early read.** Training track_ratio_mean over its 800-1000 must be ≥ 0.58, the CHARTER's FAST early-read threshold (side_bisect/scripts/early_read.py:5-6). Otherwise stop at it 1000 (~0.4 GPU-h).
- **Final.** FAST on both hands with odd RMS ≥ 1.4 (ROOT_CAUSE P3, :394). Otherwise go to the policy-switch or distillation fallbacks (:505-509), NOT to algorithm work.
- **FB_canon.** Forward tripod and fwd/back ratios must be within guard R of the t3 record, 0.558/0.524 (:499).

findings.finding: Rung 2's geometry gates (saturation share, P10) are circular: a bound loss lowers |μ| by construction. The literature and this plant's physics both predict the deterministic executed controller will barely change. A bound at 1.1, or a tanh, lets μ sit at ±1, which executes the same sign(μ) controller. Slew-limited rods get their full stroke from full-scale targets. No evidence-backed path leads from rung 2 to a task-metric gain.
findings.evidence:
Literature:
- 'a tanh head will likely converge near ±1' (lit-review-rl-algorithm-and-ppo-hyperparameters.md:171).
- 'Expect geometry to move reliably and return inconsistently' (:136).
- He et al.'s bounded penalties return 465-484 vs 594 (:103).
- Tang: tanh on the mean ties, 4007±698 vs 3905±502 (:112).
- Geiß: 'did not pay dividends' (:75).
- The legged positives are weak: GPO seeds unreported, DHAL 4 seeds (:120, :128-130, :532).
- Near-bang-bang is expected under L1-like costs (:145-150). The shipped action_rate is the unsquared L2 norm (rewards.py:337-340), so the review's 'squared action_rate' (:174) is inaccurate for the default path.

Plant:
- Rods are slew-limited at 28/33 mm/s; cams have a 2π rad/s² acceleration limit (DOSSIER.md:157).
- The lift ceiling was measured as action scale × slew (analytic 4.6 cm vs 4.2-4.7 measured), and authority 0.4's survival cost was 'intrinsic, not transitional' (I1-cont completion 0.27) (gait_formation_v2/CHANGELOG.md:38, :43).
- Side speed depends on rod stroke amplitude, 0.077-0.113 m fast vs ≤ 0.057 slow (ROOT_CAUSE.md:82-84).
findings.recommended_change:
Treat saturation share (|μ|>1.1 ≤ 0.30 at it 300) and σ gradient liveness only as a MECHANISM check that kills an arm for implementation failure. They are never a success gate.

Success requires either:
- Q block BETTER with T/F/guards at TIE or better; or
- a task block BETTER at the seed-inflated R.

Pair the arm with an executed-action total-variation/L1 cost only if smoothness is the goal (lit §4, :172-175).

findings.finding: The 3000-iteration from-scratch screens cannot measure two of the four campaign metrics. Rung 2's gates omit them, and no rung names its screen bed. Algorithm-side effects at 3k in this repo have reversed by 20k. The 50-60 GPU-h headline leaves out lineage-length confirmation, re-baselining and student re-distillation.
findings.evidence:
- Rung 2 gates: 'formation rate over seeds, tracking and side-speed class' (lit:566-567), with no turning (F/F_mt) or obstacle gate.
- Turning needs the C1d c4-c6 + c6x chain: 12k iterations, ~5.4 GPU-h per seed (DOSSIER.md:769).
- Obstacle completion needs the forward 1a→2c pipeline (crab_hex_forward_task/policy/README.md:21-25) at 1.8-2.6 GPU-h per 5k window (DOSSIER.md:768), plus the student at ~5.5 GPU-h (66.2 GPU-h over 12 runs, DOSSIER.md:677).
- 3k→20k reversal: at 3k, mirror coefficient 0.5 vs 0 gave tripod 0.573 vs 0.032; at 20k both arms were 0.0 and coefficient 0 beat 0.5 on tracking (DOSSIER.md:620-632).
- Budget claim: 'Rungs 0–8 total ≈ 50–60 GPU-h' (lit:598).
findings.recommended_change:
Name the screen bed for each rung and budget a 12k omni confirm for any rung-2 ADOPT. My arithmetic from §6 unit costs: about 16-32 GPU-h for the omni confirm and 22-31 for forward 1a→2c at 3 seeds, plus 5.5 for the student.

Cheaper alternative: add the rung-2 construction as ONE extra arm inside canonical training's P1_canon lineage (ROOT_CAUSE.md:489). That gives a full-length task read on turning at marginal cost.

findings.finding: Three seeds per cell cannot resolve the task-metric effects the literature makes plausible. Formation rate cannot improve because it is already at ceiling. Rung 2 also contradicts the review's own §11 rule that formation-rate decisions need 5 seeds. Half of the 2×2 (the two off-diagonal cells) consists of cells the review itself predicts will fail.
findings.evidence:
Seed dominance:
- Turning blocks: F R_seed 3.194 vs R_eval 0.967; F_mt 4.118 vs 0.936.
- Single-seed MDE: turn facing 0.145, move_turn facing 0.180 (facing_tracking_ladder/CHANGELOG.md:46-47).
- My arithmetic: pooling 3 seeds shrinks the seed term by at most √3, giving roughly 0.08 at 95 % and roughly 0.12 at 80 % power, and more with a t-correction because R_seed is one s2-s3 draw (DOSSIER.md:399). That is the same order as the largest curriculum effect (+0.20).
- The literature expectation is −20 % to 0, i.e. −0.16 to 0 at W's 0.787.

Formation:
- The review's own rule: 5 seeds when formation decides; 3/3 vs 0/3 gives p = 0.10 (lit:451-453).
- No headroom: 6 omni t3 runs all formed (fwd survival 0.49-0.96, five at 0.71-0.96; DOSSIER.md:403).
- The live formation failure is only the never-clocked Z (0/2 seeds; DOSSIER.md:560). It is moot because W removes the clock after formation.

Off-diagonals: 'The two knobs must be co-varied: lowering σ alone cannot produce an interior mean ... a bound alone at σ 2.0 leaves the clip binding' (lit:567-569).
findings.recommended_change:
Run the diagonal cell only (3 seeds ≈ 3.5 GPU-h). Reuse the existing incumbent t3 seeds if code_sha is unchanged; this requires rung 0's behaviour changes to be default-off. Run the off-diagonals only to explain a diagonal task-metric win; this saves ~7 GPU-h. Formation becomes a non-inferiority guard, not a success gate.

Kill criterion at its 800-1000: training track_ratio_move_mean and episode length must not fall below the lowest incumbent seed at the same iterations by more than the incumbents' own spread.

findings.finding:
σ, the LR schedule and mean saturation do not select the side-speed class. The absorbing σ clamp binds only about 1700-2300 iterations after the class is decided.

One ordering exists: at it 600, every two-direction arm has σ above every fast arm. This looks like a symptom, the entropy push going unopposed when the surrogate gradient cancels across hands.

Whether rungs 2-3 matter for side speed at all depends on C_40, which is queued now. The one concrete σ→task pathway is that RSI is inert under σ 1.5.
findings.evidence:
Computed from S/omni_stroke_side/tb_arms.json (17 arms):

| telemetry | fast | two-direction | phantom |
|---|---|---|---|
| σ at it 300 | 1.617-1.643 | 1.629-1.697 | 1.575-1.664 |
| σ at it 600 | ≤ 1.700 | ≥ 1.704 | 1.610-1.737 (overlap) |
| LR at it 300 | 4.19-4.87e-5 | — | — |
| LR at the floor | 0.33-0.38 | — | — |

- LR at it 300 is 3.48-6.38e-5 across all slow arms (phantom and two-direction); floor share is 0.31-0.41 slow.
- σ first reaches 1.99 at it 2267-2850 in fast runs, while the classes separate at ~540 (ROOT_CAUSE.md:222-227).
- Rod-mean saturation past 1+2σ is 0.01-0.06 at it 300, the same in both classes; 'Saturation or std as the selector' is ruled out (ROOT_CAUSE.md:248-252, :372).
- RSI starts underperform normal spawns even in fast C_mo (failure 0.127 vs 0.021), consistent with 'RSI is inert at init std 1.5' (:213-218, :253-256).
- C_40 pre-registered readings (side_bisect/CHARTER.md:666-673). C_fa (X21) started training at 15:15 (logs/rsl_rl/crab_hex_omni_flat_walk/2026-09-30_15-15-37_seed3_X21_s1_A15pB); C_40 runs next.
findings.recommended_change:
Pre-register the C_40 dependency:
- **C_40 FAST with moving ratio ≥ 0.58 by it 800:** drop side speed from the rung-2 and rung-3 gates entirely.
- **C_40 SLOW or FAST-late:** keep one σ-axis arm aimed at the formation window (its 0-600) on a two-direction bed.

Kill criterion for that arm: by it 500, the RSI-start failure rate must be within 0.02 of the normal-spawn rate, and moving ratio at its 800-1000 must be ≥ 0.58. Otherwise the σ pathway to side speed is dead.

findings.finding: Symmetry augmentation 'over the full 1,149-dim obs' with the omni image set feeds M_y images into RL. The in-repo root cause predicts this gives the SLOW side gait. It also conflicts with rung 7, which must keep M_y images off side rows. The forward mirror-loss formation gain did not replicate across seeds.
findings.evidence:
- Rung 6 spec (lit:584-586).
- Every network trained on both hands, from real −y data or from the mirror loss's phantom −y rows (O, R, C_band, C_rsi), is SLOW (ROOT_CAUSE.md:32-39, :145-171).
- Canonical training requires 'Keep the fa mirror. M_y images would bring the phantom −y rows back' (ROOT_CAUSE.md:486), and masks M_y to |vy_b| < h in FB_canon (:488).
- Mirror-on E1 seeds scored tripod 0.541/0.0/0.026/0.0, and E5 mirror-off (0.257) beats 3 of 4 (DOSSIER.md:635-636).
- Mirror type makes no difference once −y is sampled: LRfa and LR4 are both SLOW (DOSSIER.md:641).
- The largest algorithm-side task effect in the record is the image-set change 4-image → fa (DOSSIER.md:639).
findings.recommended_change:
Move rung 6 after rung 7. Restrict it to the M_x (fore-aft) image, loss vs augmentation, inside the canonical architecture. Drop the M_y-image augmentation arm.

Kill criterion: the arm must beat the mirror-loss arm on fwd/back ratio and tripod at 3 seeds (5 if formation decides), or stop.

findings.finding: The ladder has no stop rule, only escalation. It moves on to more heads (ordinal, GPO, FPO++) and then off-policy exactly when rung 2 moves geometry but not task metrics. After the construction is fixed, that outcome is evidence the optimizer is not the limiter. Escalating on a null invites the maximisation bias the review itself warns about.
findings.evidence:
- Rung 9: 'only if rung 2 moves geometry but not task metrics' (lit:594-596).
- The review's own warnings: guard against maximisation bias, and top seeds can come from unstable configurations (lit:417-418, citing Patterson [105] and Eimer [106]).
- The off-policy analogue is slower and more seed-variable (lit:363-367).
- PPO wall-clock is not binding: 90 % of final reward by median it 1344-1798 (DOSSIER.md:489); ~1.1 GPU-h per 3k arm (DOSSIER.md:767); learner ~20 % of wall time (DOSSIER.md:782).

findings.finding: The step-size rung targets the late, saturated regime. There, fresh optimizer state did not rescue the nulls, and a throttled optimizer still produced large task moves. During formation the controller already behaves as designed. The only controlled evidence for this rung spans zero. Its one plausible payoff is late convergence speed or late-lineage modifiability. It should be conditional, not a standing rung.
findings.evidence:
Formation:
- LR 3-6× higher; 'KL is mostly behavioural, so there the controller is doing roughly what it is designed to do' (DOSSIER.md:251, :265).
- Behavioural KL share 0.70-0.79 at it 300 (DOSSIER.md:94).

C14 (DOSSIER.md:462-471):
- From-scratch stroke/posture arms had LR at the floor only 23-37 % of the time (peaks 3.8-5.8e-4) and still FAILED.
- Throttled c6x moved turn facing 0.475→0.787.

Controlled evidence: the rl_games 3-seed study, fixed 19.6/18.9/18.9 vs legacy 18.8/18.2/18.9, with a CI spanning −0.1 to +1.0 (lit:224-228). The review itself: 'matters mainly through what the KL measures' (lit:610-612).

Possible payoff:
- omni fwd ratio 0.733→0.785 over 4000 more iterations (DOSSIER.md:487);
- forward late windows 94-99 % at the floor (DOSSIER.md:235);
- the clearance-learning plasticity cliff at 20k (crab_hex_forward_task/experiments/lit-review-plasticity-cliff.md:10-18). The pipeline of record stops at 20k.
findings.recommended_change:
Run only if the rung-2 diagonal is ADOPTed. Test on that head in the late regime (a 2000-iteration fork or its 1500-3000 window) with fixed LR 1e-4 plus a per-epoch KL early stop.

Kill criteria:
- **Mechanism:** executed-action change per update must reach ≥ 2× the incumbent by it 300 of the fork.
- **Task:** the training ratio/reward slope over the window must exceed the incumbent's seed band, and a final block must be BETTER.

Otherwise stop.

findings.finding: The value-side rung is motivated by a failure absent from the current pipelines. It also bundles a reward redesign (turning the reward clip off) that is not value hygiene and that the house rules require to pass the replay gate.
findings.evidence:
- The motivating collapse (bridge failure 0.00→0.90) came from the Aug-26 forward teacher hand-off (DOSSIER.md:661-664).
- The current forward pipeline has flat completion 0.92/0.85/0.81 and obstacles 0.56/0.58/0.66 across 2a/2b/2c (forward policy/README.md:22-24).
- The omni c6x boundary shock recovered by it 450-534 (DOSSIER.md:468).
- Critic reset is mixed: +0.65 at one bridge, tripod −0.15 in B1, falsified on v2 (DOSSIER.md:665-667).
- Value RMSE is 3-4 % of the value scale in flat/omni runs (DOSSIER.md:312-313).
- Clip-off: pre-clip −27.0 vs post-clip +6.4 at the start of t3; 13.6 % of W's return forgiven (DOSSIER.md:160).
findings.recommended_change:
Split the rung:
- Explained variance goes into rung 0.
- A separate critic Adam runs only if EV in the first 200 iterations after C1d stage boundaries falls well below its within-stage value, for example by more than 0.1. Otherwise do not run it.
- The reward clip moves to a reward campaign behind the offline replay gate.
- Value clip off and value normalisation stay as later conditional A/Bs.

findings.finding: Cut γ 0.995. No source ablates γ for slow multi-legged gaits. The nearest velocity-tracking evidence points toward a lower γ, and Krabby's current horizon is already longer than Humanoid-Gym's. No failure class is attributed to credit horizon. Doubling the horizon also rescales the value, which interacts with the absolute 0.2 value clip and the ≥ 0 reward clip.
findings.evidence:
- No γ ablation for slow gaits (lit:522); Seo γ 0.97 'helpful for simple velocity tracking', Raffin 0.983 (lit:274-275, :713-714); Playground 0.97 (lit:641).
- My arithmetic: Krabby's 0.99 at 50 Hz gives a 2.0 s horizon and 1.38 s half-life. Humanoid-Gym's 0.994 at 100 Hz gives 1.67 s and 1.15 s (lit:272).
- The side failure is a formation-time gradient/lock-in story (ROOT_CAUSE.md:48-61).
- move_turn is kinematically infeasible (DOSSIER.md:602).
- Value clip ±0.2 on V 2.85±0.45 (DOSSIER.md:149).
findings.recommended_change: Remove rung 8. Revisit only if rung-0 telemetry and a CPU replay show gait-cycle-scale income being discounted enough to change the walker/creeper ordering.

findings.finding: Rung 4 repeats rung 1's lever. Changing only the minibatch count barely changes executed motion. Changing num_envs invalidates every calibrated threshold in the campaign drivers, and the ladder does not budget the re-baselining.
findings.evidence:
- 16→4 minibatches changes executed change per update only 0.8-1.2× (DOSSIER.md:129, :186).
- 4× envs costs +5 % wall time (DOSSIER.md:322-326).
- R_eval/R_seed resolutions, the early-read 0.58/0.48 thresholds (early_read.py:5-6) and the timing bands (CHARTER.md:661-665) are all measured at 256 envs.
- Physics above 256 envs is untested for the 230 kg plant (DOSSIER.md:777).
- Rudin: fewer robots means a 'slow decrease in performance', i.e. mostly time-to-train (lit:260-262).

findings.finding: Rung 0 survives entirely. One caveat: splitting falls out of the time_out tag changes training targets and moves code_sha, which would re-baseline every incumbent unless it is a default-off knob. The review's suggested 'cheap audit' is already answered by the code.
findings.evidence:
- D9 bootstraps failure cutoffs as time-outs (DOSSIER.md:162, :192).
- Repo practice is knob-off byte-identical dumps (memory: clock-deprecation-campaign-active.md step 8).
